Miami Small Business SEO • Local Marketing • Leads

Small Business SEO & Digital Marketing in Miami, FL

Miami small businesses win or lose on local search: the cleaning company that shows up in the Doral map pack, the remodeler whose Kendall estimate form actually delivers, the auto shop in Hialeah whose Spanish reviews are answered. FixWebsiteIssues.com, the technical SEO and marketing division of WevTEC, helps Miami-Dade small businesses get found and get the call with local SEO, Google Maps, service pages that match the jobs you want, Google Ads where they pay, website maintenance so nothing breaks, and AI-search readiness. We work with trades, home services, automotive, restaurants, law, real estate, ecommerce, and professional services, remotely from Houston, with pricing built for a small business.

Local SEO + Maps + Service Pages + Google Ads + Maintenance | Built for Small Business Budgets | Houston-Based, Serving Miami Remotely Since 2013

Get a Free Small Business Visibility Audit
Talk With FixWebsiteIssues
What gets a Miami small business the call

What Can We Help Your Miami Small Business Improve?

Six outcomes, each measurable, priced for a business that watches every dollar.

Google Maps Presence

A complete, consistent Business Profile in the neighborhoods you serve, with the categories and reviews that decide the map pack.

Service Pages That Match Jobs

One page per service you actually sell, written the way customers search, so the site ranks and the calls are the right ones.

A Website That Works

Fast on a phone, forms that deliver, click-to-call, and a monthly maintenance check so it stays that way.

Reviews & Reputation

A review cadence and responses in English and Spanish, never fabricated.

Google Ads Where They Pay

Emergency and high-ticket services with tight geography and call tracking, or no Ads if the numbers do not work.

AI Search Readiness

Clear business and service information so AI assistants can understand and reference you when customers ask.

What Small Business Marketing in Miami Involves

Small business marketing in Miami is mostly local search done right: a Google Business Profile that wins the map pack in the neighborhoods you serve, a website with a page for each service written in the customer’s words, forms and a phone number that work on a phone, reviews that keep coming and get answered, Google Ads only where the cost per lead makes sense, and maintenance so an update never takes the site down. It is smaller in scope than an enterprise program and far more sensitive to the basics being wrong.

Miami adds two things. Neighborhood identity is strong, so a business is found for “Kendall” or “Doral” rather than “Miami”, and service-area businesses need coverage across the county without duplicating pages. And a large share of customers search and review in Spanish; for trades, automotive, and services in Hialeah, Doral, Kendall, and west Miami-Dade, professionally written Spanish pages and answered Spanish reviews are often the difference. We recommend Spanish content when the data supports it, never as filler.

The SEO discipline in depth is on our Miami SEO services page; the coordinated program is on the Miami digital marketing hub; keeping the site working is Miami website maintenance. National small-business guidance: small business marketing strategies.

What a small business engagement usually includes

  • Local service keyword and neighborhood research
  • Business Profile optimization and review cadence
  • Site speed and mobile fixes
  • One page per service, in English and Spanish where justified
  • Service-area content that is not duplicated
  • Lead forms and call tracking in one dashboard
  • Google Ads where the cost per lead works
  • Monthly website maintenance from $300
  • AI-search readiness: clear entity and service information

Marketing by Trade and Business Type in Miami

Each business type is found differently. These are the ones we work with most and what shapes the plan for each.

Trade

Cleaning Companies

Residential, commercial janitorial, post-construction, and pressure washing compete on instant-quote forms and the map pack across neighborhoods. Priorities: quote forms tested monthly, service-area pages that are not duplicates, Spanish reviews answered.

Trade

Remodeling & Kitchen-Bath

Long research phases, portfolio-heavy pages that slow the site, estimate conversion. Priorities: image compression, project pages with real detail, license and insurance clarity, Ads for high-ticket kitchen and bath jobs.

Trade

Construction & General Contractors

Commercial credibility for bid requests: project galleries, certifications, RFQ forms with upload, and security hardening against spam injection.

Construction SEO →

Trade

HVAC

Emergency and seasonal demand across Miami-Dade; repair versus install intent; service-area coverage; phone-first conversion; Ads during peak season.

Trade

Plumbing

“Open now” and emergency intent decided in Maps within minutes; reviews and hours accuracy; Ads for emergency calls with strict geography.

Trade

Roofing

Storm-driven spikes, insurance-claim questions, and high-trust, high-ticket decisions; credibility signals and fast response paths matter most.

Trade

Automotive

Repair, body, tire, and detailing searches; booking integrations, inventory feeds, hours accuracy, and bilingual reviews in Hialeah and Doral.

Automotive SEO →

Business

Restaurants & Hospitality

Cuisine and neighborhood intent on Miami Beach, Wynwood, and Brickell; menu visibility, reservation and ordering integrations, reviews on Maps.

Retail and hospitality SEO →

Business

Law Firms

Practice-area pages, attorney profiles, expensive competitive terms, and the trust signals clients look for; Spanish for immigration and personal injury where justified.

Law firm SEO →

Business

Real Estate

Neighborhood and property-type intent, agent pages, listings that expire, and IDX integrations that create technical debt; Latin American buyer audiences.

Business

Ecommerce

WooCommerce and Shopify: category architecture, faceted-navigation bloat, product schema, speed, and checkout tested with a live order.

Business

Professional Services

Accountants, consultants, insurance and financial advisors: expertise-driven content, service pages, and trust signals over volume.

Local SEO and Google Maps for Miami Small Businesses

For most small businesses the first call comes from Google Maps. Maps ranks on relevance, distance, and prominence: the right categories and services on the Business Profile, consistent business information across the web, reviews and responses, and a website that supports the listing. Organic rankings and Maps rankings need overlapping but different work, and proximity is a factor no agency controls, so we do not promise map-pack positions.

Service-area businesses that travel to customers have a specific problem: they need to be found across Miami-Dade without ten duplicate neighborhood pages. The answer is a correctly configured service-area Business Profile, a few genuinely different area pages, and content that names the neighborhoods naturally. Common findings on Miami small business listings: wrong or missing categories, a home address shown when it should be hidden, hours that differ from the site, Spanish reviews unanswered, and a duplicate listing created by a former employee.

Small business local SEO covers

  • Business Profile setup, categories, services, attributes
  • Service-area configuration for businesses that travel
  • Consistent name, address, phone, hours everywhere
  • Review cadence and responses in English and Spanish
  • Citations on local and trade directories
  • A few real area pages instead of many duplicates
  • Duplicate listing cleanup
  • Call tracking without breaking consistency
  • Maps visibility monitoring by service and neighborhood

Google Ads for Miami Small Businesses

Google Ads pays for a small business when the service is urgent or high-ticket, the geography is tight, and every call is tracked. It loses money when it targets the whole county, sends clicks to the homepage, and counts clicks instead of leads. We say no to Ads when the cost per lead does not work, and we run it alongside SEO when it does, so the owner sees cost per lead by channel.

Efficient small business campaigns are specific: one campaign per service, geography around the neighborhoods you actually serve, Spanish campaigns with Spanish landing pages where justified, negative keywords that remove job seekers and DIY searches, landing pages that match the ad, and call and form tracking.

Keep the Site Working

A small business rarely has anyone watching the site, which is why maintenance is part of the plan: updates on staging first, backups, security, and a monthly check that forms deliver and the phone number works. Plans from $300 per month; details on the Miami website maintenance page. If the site is hacked or down, Miami hacked website repair comes first.

Small Business Marketing Across Miami-Dade

Where Miami small business customers search and what shapes the plan in each area. All work is remote; FixWebsiteIssues has no Miami office.

Doral and Hialeah

Trades, automotive, logistics, and services with predominantly Spanish-speaking customers. Spanish pages, reviews, and Business Profile content are frequently decisive.

Kendall and West Kendall

Home services, cleaning, remodeling, and consumer businesses serving large residential neighborhoods; Maps presence and quote forms drive most first calls.

Brickell, Downtown, and Coconut Grove

Professional services, restaurants, retail, and wellness for a dense, review-conscious population; reviews and precise location signals decide.

Coral Gables and South Miami

Established professional services, real estate, and legal practices; credentials and consistency outperform promotions.

Miami Beach and Wynwood

Hospitality, restaurants, and retail with seasonal, multilingual demand; hours, reviews, and speed carry unusual weight.

Aventura and North Miami

Retail and services with affluent customers and competition from Broward; location precision keeps Broward businesses from winning Aventura searches.

Also serving Homestead, Cutler Bay, Palmetto Bay, Pinecrest, Sweetwater, Miami Lakes, and the rest of Miami-Dade, plus Broward and Palm Beach counties.

What Small Business Marketing Cannot Guarantee

  • No agency controls rankings, map-pack positions, or AI mentions; proximity is outside anyone’s control.
  • Leads depend on pricing, availability, reviews, and how the phone is answered, not marketing alone.
  • Google Ads only pays for some services and some budgets; we say so when it does not.
  • Spanish content helps only when the business can serve customers in Spanish.
  • We do not publish case studies without client approval; that section is in progress.
Example methodology, not a case study

How We Would Approach a Kendall Remodeling Contractor

Situation. A kitchen-and-bath remodeler with a 300-image portfolio, an estimate form, a Business Profile listing the owner’s home address, and a site that takes nine seconds to load on a phone. Leads have slowed.

Likely findings. No separate kitchen, bath, or addition pages; the estimate form sending to an old address; an abandoned gallery plugin; no Spanish content despite half the calls being in Spanish; the home address visible on Maps when it should be a service area.

Sequence. Fix the form and Business Profile, hide the address, set the service area (week 1). Compress the portfolio and replace the gallery plugin (weeks 1 to 2). Build kitchen, bath, and addition pages with real project detail and financing (weeks 2 to 6). Add Spanish versions of the top three (weeks 5 to 8). Launch a kitchen-remodel Ads campaign around Kendall and Pinecrest (week 4). Track estimates by source and language.

Measurement. Estimate requests by source, Business Profile calls, service-page visibility, Ads cost per estimate. Structure, not a promised result.

Is Your Miami Small Business Showing Up Where Customers Look?

We will check your Maps presence, service pages, site speed, forms, and AI visibility for free and tell you what to fix first.

  • Website repair depth: the broken form, the slow gallery, and the hacked site are fixed by our engineers, not reported.
  • Trade and service-industry experience with cleaning, remodeling, construction, HVAC, plumbing, roofing, automotive, and restaurants.

What does small business marketing in Miami involve?

Local search done right: a Business Profile that wins the map pack, a page per service in the customer’s words, a fast site with working forms and click-to-call, reviews answered in English and Spanish, Google Ads only where the cost per lead works, and maintenance so nothing breaks. Measured in tracked calls and quote requests.

How much does it cost?

Website maintenance starts at $300 per month. SEO and Ads are scoped to what the business can use, typically a few hundred to a couple of thousand dollars per month combined. We quote after a free audit; there is no single package price.

Do I need Google Ads?

Only if the service is urgent or high-ticket, the geography is tight, and calls are tracked. We say no when the cost per lead does not work and run it alongside SEO when it does.

Should I create pages for every neighborhood?

No. A correctly configured service-area Business Profile, a few genuinely different area pages, and content that names neighborhoods naturally outperform ten duplicate pages, which weaken the whole site.

Do Spanish pages help my business?

Often, in Hialeah, Doral, Kendall, and west Miami-Dade, when the business can serve customers in Spanish. Professionally written Spanish pages and answered Spanish reviews are frequently the difference; machine translation is never used.

Can you fix my existing website?

Yes. Most small business clients come with a site built elsewhere. We fix speed, forms, security, and structure without a forced redesign, and maintain it from $300 per month.

How do reviews affect my visibility?

Strongly. Reviews influence Maps prominence, conversion, and what AI assistants say about a business. We set up a cadence, respond in both languages, and never fabricate or filter.

Which trades and business types do you work with?

Cleaning, remodeling, construction, HVAC, plumbing, roofing, automotive, restaurants and hospitality, law firms, real estate, ecommerce, and professional services, each with a plan shaped to how it is found.

Can you promise map-pack results?

No. Proximity is a Maps factor no one controls. We remove the reasons a competitor would be preferred and measure what changes.

How can a small business appear in AI search?

By being clear, consistent, and corroborated: what you do, where you serve, who you are, and reviews and listings that agree. It improves the likelihood of being understood and referenced; nothing guarantees a mention.

Do you have an office in Miami?

No. FixWebsiteIssues is based in Houston, Texas, and serves Miami-Dade businesses remotely with secure access.

How do you measure success?

Tracked calls, quote requests, and bookings by source and language; Business Profile actions; service-page visibility by neighborhood; Ads cost per lead; review velocity; and recorded AI visibility observations.
